# Embassy v1.4.1

A same-night hotfix for v1.4.0. Claude Code 2.1.227 rolled out onto machines that were working minutes earlier, and Embassy's exact-version launcher gate stopped `embassy serve` from starting at all. v1.4.0 could not run on an up-to-date machine, so this release exists to make the general-availability release actually available.

**The Claude Code pin moves to 2.1.227**

- The upgrade was verified before the pin moved rather than assumed. A live 2.1.227 registry record carries the same closed field set and `peerProtocol: 1`, and publishes the same mode-0600 `/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` under a 0700 directory. Comparing the 2.1.226 and 2.1.227 builds directly, the registry writer and reader, the newline-delimited JSON framing and its 1 MiB no-newline cap, the inbound user-frame acceptance rules, and the `peer_message_status` frame shape are unchanged apart from minifier renames and an internal refactor.
- Still-running 2.1.224 through 2.1.226 sessions remain discoverable during the patch-upgrade overlap.

**The drift message stops promising a fix that does not exist**

- It said the installed Claude Code was newer than this build supports and to run `npm update -g agent-embassy`. Updating does nothing when no published Embassy supports the installed Claude Code yet — which is the first case anyone hits, because the maintainer hits it before a release exists. The message now names both outcomes and tells the operator how to tell them apart.
- It also no longer asserts the installed build is "newer". The gate is exact equality, so drift is possible in either direction.

**Compatibility pins** — Claude Code 2.1.227 (peer protocol 1), managed standalone App Server 0.147.0, Node.js ≥ 20, macOS only.

Upgrading from v1.4.0 needs nothing. If `embassy serve` was refusing to start with `CLAUDE_VERSION_DRIFT`, this release is the fix.
